shared_elements: shallow incised or low-relief carving on weathered stone
vertical parallel line groups (garment- or hair-like hatching)
raised curving elements resembling arms or limbs
justification: Both are upright stone monuments bearing shallow schematic carving in which a central disc sits above a horizontal banded zone and below vertically hatched, hair- or garment-like fields, and both use simple anthropomorphic line-drawing rather than modelled anatomy. The decisive difference is scale and format: A is a thin flat pointed slab densely filled with multiple small figures in stacked registers, while B is a massive three-dimensional block whose sparse carving articulates a single body, so the compositional schemes correspond only in generic vertical stacking.
